claims.claim: Gregory Thaumaturgus was a Christian bishop of Neocaesarea in Pontus (modern Niksar, Turkey) in the 3rd century.
Gregory Thaumaturgus was born around AD 213 and died around AD 270.
Gregory Thaumaturgus studied with Origen at Caesarea in Palestine for five years (probably 233–238), where he was converted to Christianity.
Gregory Thaumaturgus was originally named Theodore and came from a pagan family.
Gregory Thaumaturgus was made bishop of Neocaesarea by Phaedimus of Amasea, who ordained him in his absence while Gregory was hiding in the wilderness.
The Declaration of Faith is one of the earliest formal declarations of Trinitarian faith from the third century.
The title of the work includes the claim that Gregory had it 'by revelation from the blessed John the evangelist, by the mediation of the Virgin Mary, Parent of God.'
